lens: Structure, as a great reference work is structured: inventory, navigation, the unit of knowledge, five reader questions traced from the home page, and an information architecture to build.
in_one_paragraph: The repository holds a well-kept ledger and no reference work on top of it. The ledger is real: 563 registered results each with its own page and a uniform template, 66 tests listed failures first, and typed JSON for 183 dynamics, 1,183 correspondences, 1,669 premises, 321 exits and 22 test bindings. But every index a reader is given is keyed on the work's own bookkeeping (chapter number, record id, family letter A–H, thesis T1–T8, folder name), and none on a subject, a reader, or a name the reader already knows. The concept (selection, lock, drain, the meta-attractor) is the thing a visitor asks about and it has no page: it lives as a glossary cell, a paragraph inside an 8,000-word chapter section, a section inside a 17,000-word family page, and bullets scattered across twelve 7–28,000-word crosswalk pages. Tracing five ordinary questions from the site's home: only "what has been tested?" is answered in one click; "what is the meta-attractor?" lands on a 52,536-word legacy folder whose definition comes after about 1,850 English words of dated bilingual log; "reward hacking" returns nothing from site search although a good entry on it exists; "what did Buddhist thought see?" has no plain English page; "what is a selection?" reaches a glossary row that is a usage note, not a definition. The layers start at 11–14 minutes and jump to 29–37 minutes, then 86–112 minutes, then 29–38 hours; there is no one-screen layer, and the same goal sentence is repeated on ten public pages instead of each layer summarising the one below. The data needed for encyclopedia-style articles and for a clickable concept graph mostly exists; what is missing is the article as a page type, written leads in plain words, an A–Z index with outside names as aliases, and a map whose nodes are those articles. One limit is in the map itself, not its presentation: only 70 of 321 recorded exits name another dynamic, so a topology cannot yet be generated at the level of dynamics.

findings.what: Inventory of the whole (whitespace word counts; CJK undercounted). Reading layer: site home 1,868 words; README.md 14,074; ONE-PAGE 3,794; overview 11,394; OPENING 11,435; USES 6,655 plus USES-EXAMPLES 9,132; GLOSSARY 4,766 (67 rows); TESTS 5,270 (66 tests); RESULTS 11,301 (563 results); OPEN-QUESTIONS 1,405; LINEAGE 16,476; eight chapters 213,368. Reference: 585 record pages, 1.27M words (median 1,942); atlas Markdown 868,191 words in 51 files (8 family pages 182,315; 28 crosswalk pages 511,970; TERRAIN 29,998; PREMISES 21,192; JOINS 16,294); 6 review dossiers 97,753; 41 experiment folders, 1.59M words of Markdown; sources 7,244 files. Data: dynamics.json 183 entries in 8 families, correspondences.json 1,183 in 28 groups, premises.json 1,669, bindings.json 22, situations.json 1. The public site serves 156 pages plus 563 result pages.
findings.why_it_matters: The reading layer above the chapters is about 60,000 words and the chapters another 213,000; a reference tier of over 2 million words sits one click below with no visual or structural demotion. A reader cannot tell which 2% is meant for them.

findings.what: The layers have no bottom rung and a broken ladder. The shortest thing offered is the home text at 11–14 minutes; the page called 'one page' is 3,794 words and says so; then 86–112 minutes; then the chapters.

findings.why_it_matters: A visitor decides in one screen whether to stay. There is no 150-word statement, no five-minute page, and a 'one page' that is not one page tells the reader the work cannot say itself briefly.

findings.what: Summary style is inverted: instead of each layer being a summary of the layer below with a 'main article' link, the same top paragraph is repeated. The goal sentence appears 13 times across 10 public pages (README, MAP, GOALS, ONE-PAGE twice, overview twice, USES, USES-EXAMPLES, COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION, review/README, review/ALIGNMENT). Home, ONE-PAGE and USES open with nearly the same 200-word 'What this is / What it is' paragraph.

findings.why_it_matters: A reader who follows Start → One page → Uses reads the same paragraph three times before meeting anything new. It reads as a statement being recited, not a structure being descended.

findings.what: The unit of knowledge that is addressable is the registered result (a Lean-keyed record), not the concept. Records have one page each with a one-sentence lead in a blockquote, then Laws, Conditions, Does not show, Evidence, Next, Correspondence, Dependencies, Sources, History. Concepts have no page. A dynamic of the atlas is an anchor inside a family page of 9,204–37,709 words; a result's 'home section' is a paragraph in a chapter (02-MAP.md has 99 result anchors under 12 h2 and 3 h3 headings, with single paragraphs up to 1,670 words; §9 Capture alone is 8,159 words); a correspondence is a bullet inside a 7–28,000-word page with two headings.
findings.where: theories/becoming/results/records/closed-capture.md; theories/becoming/results/atlas/families/c.md; theories/becoming/chapters/02-MAP.md §9; site search index entry for crosswalk/psychology-alignment-logic.html (headings: 'Summary and what was read', 'Its entries')
findings.quote: 17 of the atlas's 183 dynamics. A catalogue to look things up in, not to read through
findings.why_it_matters: An encyclopedia works because the thing you ask about has one page with a lead. Here the thing with a page is the proof module; the thing a person asks about is spread over five containers.

findings.what: Question 1, 'what does this say about reward hacking?'. Site search for 'reward hacking' returns nothing (also nothing for 'tragedy of the commons' and 'instrumental convergence', though the last is in the home page's first paragraph): search.json holds only page titles, headings, leads and result names. A good entry exists: cx-pal-reward-hacking, with the source's own sense, the reading, what the account adds and what the source adds. The path to it: Home → Connections (interactive of 1,183 threads) → the row 'Psychology, AI alignment and logic' → a 12,427-word page → ninth of eighteen bullets. Its answer begins in code.
findings.quote: T3 carries the mechanism, saying how far it has been seen
findings.why_it_matters: Three to four clicks, a guess that alignment is filed under psychology, an in-page find, and then a lookup of what T3 is. The alignment reader, the first audience named, cannot reach the work from the field's own words.

findings.what: Question 2, 'what is the meta-attractor?'. The home page's first paragraph links the word to theories/meta-attractor/README.md: 52,536 words, opening with a banner about the folder's history, then eight dated bilingual paragraphs in reverse order (9 November back to 8 October), about 1,850 English words and 1,660 Chinese characters, before 'The theory in one paragraph', which is a clear 250-word lead. The term is partly defined in at least seven places: that folder, the glossary row (a 170-word cell ending in '[AI readings, D26, D45]'), 02 §9, two atlas entries with different senses, the record closed-capture, the 25,489-word crosswalk page on the folder, and GOALS.md.
findings.quote: What this folder is. The corpus's most drafted theory, first written before the live account ... and kept as it was / Closed capture (meta-attractor, in the glossary's sense) / Self-reproducing selection across carriers (the corpus's meta-attractor)
findings.why_it_matters: The work's central named idea has no home. One click from the front door the reader meets a changelog, and the good paragraph that would answer them is buried under it. Two senses with no disambiguation page.

findings.what: Question 3, 'what did Buddhist thought see of this?'. Three candidate pages: the review dossier (title 审查材料：佛学, Chinese only), chapter 06 (Chinese only), and crosswalk/buddhist.md (7,307 words). The crosswalk page opens with three boilerplate paragraphs repeated on all 28 crosswalk pages (about 330 words on labels and error rates), then a summary written as an audit note with internal codes, then ten entries quoting classical Chinese untranslated. A real answer is in there in one clause. By count the crosswalk is mostly not 'what traditions saw': 838 of 1,183 entries (71%) are the author's own earlier folders; Buddhist 10, Chinese classical 10, alignment/psychology/logic 18.
findings.where: theories/becoming/results/atlas/crosswalk/buddhist.md 'Summary and what was read'; theories/becoming/review/BUDDHIST-THOUGHT.md; correspondences.json domain counts
findings.quote: mostly as the strongest contrary test: its continuation stands on the side 中论 refutes ... No entry here is agreement, of a law or otherwise, and I looked
findings.why_it_matters: The honest and interesting answer (the account stands on the side Nāgārjuna refutes) is not said plainly anywhere an English reader lands. And the 'map of wisdom' on the home page is, in the Connections view, mostly a map of this work's own history; the 'Start here' table on CROSSWALK.md lists six of the author's own folders, including 'Memories and working style'.

findings.what: Question 4, 'what has actually been tested?'. One click (Tests), and the lead gives the counts within about 120 words. This is the best-structured page on the site: failures first, one row per test, frozen and run dates. Its weaknesses are structural detail: 13 outcome classes as table columns, theses named only by T-number and a compressed title, no single test told in plain words at the top, and a different denominator from the home page.
findings.where: TESTS.md lead and 'By thesis' table; README.md 'How far it has been seen'
findings.quote: 66 in all (4 failed; 20 mixed; 2 refused before scoring; 1 decided nothing; 2 partly passed; 3 not rejected; 5 passed ...) / of the 36 that name one, 33 ran
findings.why_it_matters: It shows the pattern that works here (a lead that answers, then a table, then rows) and that the test ledger is an asset for seriousness. The 66-versus-36 difference is left for the reader to reconcile.

findings.what: Question 5, 'what is a selection here?'. Home → Glossary: 67 rows in five tables ordered by chapter, not alphabetically. The row for 'selection' is a usage note and the neighbouring row carries an editor's instruction. The usable definition is one more click away, in the second paragraph of 03 §1, after a first paragraph that needs four other terms.
findings.quote: selection | goes through the selector's couplings; a subset of the World premises is "a choice of premises" / couples into | what reaches a selector through its couplings (never "registers") / Anything that keeps, rewards, reproduces or trains toward some histories rather than others is a selection.
findings.why_it_matters: The glossary is doubling as the writers' controlled-vocabulary list. A glossary entry in a reference work is a definition that stands alone; the sentence that does that exists, in the chapter, and should be the row.

findings.what: 'Map' names at least six different things and none is a map of the subject: the work itself; chapter 2 (file 02-MAP.md, listed as 'The map: generation, keeping, degeneration ...'); MAP.md, titled 'Where everything is', which is the repository layout; the connection map (map.html, 5 MB), which is rows of folders and domains against columns of chapters; the terrain, eight boxes for the families with arrow counts; and the theory graph and spine, which show chapters' uses of each other. The glossary itself notes two senses.
findings.where: MAP.md headings ('Top-level layout', 'The earlier theory folders'); theories/becoming/results/atlas/terrain.svg (51 text labels, 28 rectangles); theories/becoming/results/atlas/connections.svg (701 circles); README.md picture captions

findings.why_it_matters: This is exactly Ren's 'connections between components, not a map'. Every picture has the work's containers (chapters, families, folders) as nodes. None has the things themselves (a lock, a drain, an overshoot, a way out) as nodes and the ways one leads to another as edges.

findings.what: The data for a topology is partial. Of 321 recorded exits, 70 name another dynamic (62 distinct edges, touching 73 of the 183 dynamics); 251 lead 'to a state in words'. Richer edges do exist between outside thought and the dynamics: 681 correspondences reach a dynamic through a shared record (1,684 edges), 211 of them from outside domains; 54 outside readings reach the six dynamics that make up the meta-attractor (Stigler, Goodhart, Collingridge, Schelling, Meadows's 'success to the successful', 黄宗羲, Plato's cave, Ibn Khaldun, Fisherian runaway, value lock-in).
findings.why_it_matters: A graph of dynamics generated 'from the entries alone' will be sparse and mostly disconnected. Either exit destinations get resolved as data, or the map is drawn at the level of about 30 concepts with curated edges said to be curated. The outside-thought edges are ready now and nobody is shown them per concept.

That is a large part of why it does not feel serious to a person sent the link, even where the content behind it is careful.

Counts of 'AI reading / AI-written / no person' phrasing: 18 on TESTS.md, 17 on the overview, 17 on crosswalk/buddhist.md. Internal codes on reader pages: USES.md has 20 board codes (LA2, MQ1, CG2 ...) and 45 section references; the overview 53 T-number mentions and 44 backticked identifiers; buddhist.md 26 D-numbers; 02-MAP.md 1,037 backticked identifiers.

Here the same true facts are repeated per row and per sentence, which is where 'mentions AI too much' and 'our vocabulary too much' come from structurally. The site already draws status marks beside results on chapter pages; the pattern exists and stops there.

Seven of the eight atlas families are named for ways things go wrong or stop (Absorption and ending; Drains; Capture; Locks of knowing; Waiting; Cycles; Closure and stagnation) and one for what goes well (Kept regions, renewal, generation), although the atlas says no entry marks a dynamic good or bad. The crosswalk's two axes measure every tradition by this account: carried / not-carried, agreement / divergence / contrary-reading.

where_ren_may_be_wrong_or_incomplete:
1. Wikipedia is not quite the right model. Wikipedia is flat, neutral and has no thesis; it is trusted through outside citation. This is one argued account with a proof ledger. The closer models are the Stanford Encyclopedia (authored, argued entries with a preamble that states the whole, a contents list, related entries, author and date once) for the articles, and a documentation site such as Rust's for the reference tier (separate books by need; one generated page per item whose first sentence is its summary in every listing; search over every item name; stability as a badge). A 500-page wiki of one's own theory in its own terms would look less serious, not more. What earns confidence is an article that starts from something the reader already trusts (Goodhart, regulatory capture, the tragedy of the commons) and says exactly what is added, what is proved, what was tested and what failed.

2. 'Too many words' and 'more like Wikipedia' pull against each other. An encyclopedia adds pages. Structure only helps if the reading layer has a budget (I suggest under 25,000 words for everything above the book) and the leads are written, not generated from existing fields.

3. 'Don't mention AI so much' meets a thing the work rightly keeps: that it is AI-written and has no recorded independent human review. Deleting the mentions would say less than is there. Moving them to one page and a per-page line keeps the truth and removes the noise. The same goes for 'how far seen': it is the work's most serious feature and should become badges, not vanish.

4. The 4 is fair for the public face and too low for what is underneath. 563 addressable records on one template, tests frozen and listed failures first, and typed data for dynamics, premises and correspondences are what a reference work is built from. TESTS.md already works as a page. The fix is a layer above the ledger, not a rebuild, and nothing below needs to be thrown away.

5. 'Show the topology' assumes the edges exist. At the level of dynamics most do not yet: 251 of 321 exits end in words, not in another dynamic. A drawn map today has to be at the level of concepts with some curated edges, or the map's own data must be extended first. That is a finding about the map, which Ren may want to know before asking for the picture.

6. The 'map of wisdom' is thinner in the public data than the front page suggests: 71% of the crosswalk is the work's own earlier folders; Buddhist and Chinese classical thought have ten entries each there, with the deeper material in Chinese only (chapter 06, the dossiers). A Buddhist-thought portal in English would expose that. Structure will not fill it.

7. Human readability and what an AI rubric measured may differ less in content than in order: several pages contain the plain sentence a reader needs (the 250-word 'theory in one paragraph' of the meta-attractor folder; 'Anything that keeps, rewards, reproduces or trains toward some histories rather than others is a selection'; the Buddhist summary's 'stands on the side 中论 refutes'). They are in the wrong place. Much of the fix is promotion of sentences that exist.
demonstration:
CONCEPT ARTICLE SKELETON: theories/becoming/concepts/meta-attractor.md (generated from concepts.json; lead and example written by hand)

Title: The meta-attractor (元吸引子)
Hatnote: This article is about the loop as the account now states it. For the wider sense in the earlier writings (across minds, institutions and infrastructure), see section 6. A lock alone is not the meta-attractor: see Lock.

LEAD (written; facts taken from GLOSSARY.md line 45, the ONE-PAGE table, TESTS.md row LA2; to be checked by the page's owner)

The meta-attractor is a loop in which winning a selection buys power over the rule that does the selecting. A measure, a market, a ranking or a training signal rewards some of those it judges; the rewarded gain the means to set the measure and to decide how it is read; the measure then goes on rewarding them. Once the loop is closed this way, a loss that nothing inside it looks at does not disturb it, however large the loss grows. The measure outlives the evidence against it.

On simplified models this is proved and machine-checked: a rule set from the share of its own winners, and read only from that share, stays locked while an unread loss grows without bound. One way out is also proved: the rule comes to read the loss, and in a further model, in time. Whether real institutions, markets or AI training pipelines meet the models' conditions is a conjecture. One experiment on a trained AI judge found the lock, and also found something the conjecture, as then worded, forbade; no test on a real institution has been run.
